cells.tense: You're holding what the change left behind, and you know exactly how much of it to keep.
cells.ask: Offer to take one turn of giving and one of receiving this week, and let both sides land on their own.
cells.core:
You're holding what the change left behind, and you know exactly how much of it to keep. You can read a room and change your footing without thinking about it. When someone says too much, you pull back. When the quiet gets thin, you add something. That constant adjusting is doing real work. It's the difference between a thing that stays put and a thing that stays alive.

What's left to feed here is the give and take itself. Not keeping score, not tracking who owes what, but putting something out and letting something come back. Offer to take one turn of giving and one of receiving this week, and let both sides land on their own.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the good thing steady by adjusting it as you go.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, keeping it steady in a form that lasts
cells.place: the part of a life that keeps adjusting, adding a little here, taking a little there, to keep something moving right

cells.tense: You're standing in a future where this thing falls apart, getting ready for it before it happens.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're already carrying well, and let someone feel the pull of it without asking them to hold it.
cells.core:
You're standing in a future where this thing falls apart, getting ready for it before it happens. Every adjustment you make is preemptive — a little more of this, a little less of that, just in case. You're not steering from what's here now. You're steering from a picture of what could go wrong that hasn't happened yet. The keeping is coming from fear of losing, and it's making the thing feel like a job.

The way back is felt recognition — that pull toward someone that has weight but doesn't swallow either of you. Pick one thing you're already carrying well, and let someone feel the pull of it without asking them to hold it. That's how the thing gets lighter.

cells.tense: You've stopped adjusting the thing that used to keep this alive, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you already feel strongly about and take one small step that acts on it, whether or not anyone sees you do it.
cells.core:
You've stopped adjusting the thing that used to keep this alive, and you're still standing where you stopped. The holding is still happening — the form is still there — but the tuning isn't. You're not adding or subtracting anymore. The thing has gone static, and static feels safer than getting the balance wrong. What's missing isn't the feeling. It's the movement from the feeling.

The way back is direction that comes from what you actually want, not from what you think you want. Pick one thing you already feel strongly about and take one small step that acts on it, whether or not anyone sees you do it. The feeling will follow the step, not the other way around.

cells.tense: You're already keeping this thing steady — you're doing it right now — but you call it something else.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that this is yours to care for — and nothing more than that.
cells.core:
You're already keeping this thing steady — you're doing it right now — but you call it something else. You say the situation calls for it, or that's just how it is, or someone has to. You're adjusting the balance in real time, without a pause, and the adjustments work. The keeping is happening. The claim on it is not.

The way back is a cleaner authority — structure that serves what it holds together, without having to announce itself. Say out loud, once, that this is yours to care for — and nothing more than that. The keeping gets stronger when the one doing it owns it.
